intro: You're looking for the best business wills near you because your will needs to do more than pass on personal belongings — it has to work with your company shares or partnership interest. You want someone local who understands how a business will fits alongside shareholder agreements and business relief, and who can quote you directly for that work.
need_heading: What people searching for business wills usually need
need_lead: A business will is a specialised document, and the situations that prompt the search are often tied to ownership, succession and the people left behind.
needs: You own shares in a private company and want your will to say clearly who should inherit them, rather than leaving a gap that the articles of association then fill.
You are a partner in a partnership and need your will to align with the partnership agreement, so your interest passes as the agreement intends.
You want to consider business relief and how changing rules might affect what your family receives, and you need a will that is drafted with that in mind.
You have a separate business will in mind because your personal will already deals with your home and savings, and you want the business side kept distinct.
You are reviewing an existing will that was written before you started or grew the business, and you want to check it still works with your current ownership structure.
context_heading: What to understand before you choose
context: Writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, so some will writers are not regulated. Solicitors regulated by the SRA and chartered legal executives regulated by CILEx are insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman, and many specialists are also members of STEP or Solicitors for the Elderly. When you are judging who is best for your business will, ask about regulation, professional indemnity insurance and where your original will is stored.

Business wills often need to be read alongside your articles of association or partnership agreement, and business relief rules are changing, so the drafting has to take both into account. If your business or assets are in Scotland, succession and confirmation follow different rules, so make sure your adviser practises in the right jurisdiction.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for a business will and that you want someone near you, so we can introduce you to a suitable wills and probate specialist in your area.
Describe your business structure — whether you are a sole trader, in a partnership or a company shareholder — and roughly what your interest is.
Mention whether you already have a will and whether it deals with your business interest at all.
Say whether there is a shareholder agreement or partnership agreement that your will needs to work with.
Explain whether you want a separate business will or one will covering both personal and business assets.
Note whether any business property or shares are in Scotland, so we can introduce you to someone who practises in the right jurisdiction.
questions: Are you regulated, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance for the business will work you would do for me?
How will you make sure my business will works with my company's articles of association or my partnership agreement?
What is your experience of drafting business wills that take business relief into account, given the changing rules?
Will you store my original will, and where will it be kept?
Do you recommend a separate business will alongside my personal will, and why?
If any of my business interests are in Scotland, will you handle that yourself or work with someone who practises there?

faqs.q: Why would I need a business will rather than a standard will?
faqs.a: A standard will may not deal properly with company shares or partnership interests, and it can conflict with a shareholder or partnership agreement. A business will is drafted to work with those documents and to consider business relief.

faqs.q: How do I judge who is best for a business will near me?
faqs.a: Ask whether the professional is regulated by the SRA or CILEx, holds professional indemnity insurance and has experience of business wills and the agreements that sit alongside them. You can also ask about membership of STEP or Solicitors for the Elderly, and compare quotes directly.

faqs.q: Are business relief rules changing, and does that affect my will?
faqs.a: Business relief rules are changing, and the way your will is drafted can affect how relief applies to your shares or business property. A wills and probate specialist can explain the current position and how your will should be worded.

faqs.q: Can iComply give me advice about my business will?
faqs.a: No — iComply is not regulated and does not give professional advice or provide the service itself. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who quotes you directly, and you decide whether to proceed.

extra_heading: Comparing local business will specialists on more than price
extra: Searching for the best business wills near me usually means you want a shortlist you can judge for yourself, not a ranking someone else has decided for you. Nobody can honestly promise that one practice is best for every business owner, because a will for a company shareholder raises different questions from one for a partnership. What you can do is compare how each specialist approaches your particular ownership structure.

A useful first conversation is to ask how they would read your articles of association or partnership agreement alongside the will, and whether they would draft a separate business will. Ask too how they keep the will aligned if the agreement or your shareholding changes later. The professional who asks you the most precise questions about your business is often the one worth a second conversation.

Price matters, but a quote given as POA should come with a clear description of what the work covers, so you can compare like with like. Ask whether the quote includes reviewing your existing will, the agreement and any business relief considerations, or whether those are charged separately. Comparing that scope across local specialists tells you more than comparing headline figures alone.

extra_faqs.q: Does "near me" mean I need someone in my own town?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many business will matters are handled by phone, post and secure email, so a specialist a little further away who understands your ownership structure may suit you better than the closest option. What matters is that they practise in the right jurisdiction for your business and assets.

extra_faqs.q: Should my business will be a separate document from my personal will?
extra_faqs.a: That is a decision for you and the professional, and it depends on how your business interest is held and what your existing will already covers. A separate business will can keep the business side distinct, but it also needs to be kept consistent with your personal will so the two do not pull against each other.
